title: Name artifacts as theme(:category)*:aspect(.variant)?

facts.note: Fires whenever the planner writes an artifact name: creating, renaming, or referencing/using an existing artifact by name. Applies in any document type (plans, wagons, WMBTs, acceptances, contracts, docs are non-exhaustive examples).
Task text mentions naming, referencing, or using an artifact.

values: artifact name written, changed, or referenced
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer that extracts artifact-name strings from any edited file (plans, wagons, acceptances, contracts, docs, etc.) and detects names that are added, changed, or newly referenced.

fires: Planner adds a new artifact to a wagon's produce or consume list and must name it.
Planner renames an existing artifact or introduces a variant of an existing aspect.
Planner writes or changes a reference to an existing artifact by name in a plan, WMBT, acceptance, or doc.
Planner names an artifact in a contract (e.g. its identifier or URN) with no plan or wagon change.
Planner names an artifact in any other document type.
doesNotFire: Planner edits prose in any document without writing, changing, or referencing any artifact name.
Naming of wagons themselves (covered by the wagon URN naming convention, which only shares the kebab grammar).
Code-level identifiers (functions, variables, files) that are not artifact names.

given: An artifact name is being written, changed, or referenced in any document (e.g. a plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance, contract, or doc — non-exhaustive).
when: The planner writes that artifact name or a reference to it.
then: Write the name as {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? — exactly one theme, zero or more hierarchy categories, exactly one leaf aspect, and an optional variant, every part kebab-case.
prefer: Start with the top-level architectural theme as the namespace (kebab-case ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$).
Use colons only for hierarchy (vertical depth): each category navigates one level down the resource tree; depth is unlimited.
End the colon path with the leaf resource noun as the aspect.
Use a single dot only for a variant: a lateral variation, facet, or state of the aspect (typically at most one).
Use the simple form theme:aspect when no hierarchy is needed.
avoid: Omitting the theme or the aspect, or naming with more than one theme or aspect.
Using a dot for hierarchy or a colon for a variant.
Non-kebab-case parts (uppercase, underscores, leading digits or hyphens).
why: Theme-based namespacing gives semantic clarity and collision-free names, colons give unlimited hierarchical depth and dots lateral variants, and the structure keeps artifact names aligned with contract file paths.
evidence: Every written, changed, or referenced artifact name matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)*:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)?$ (theme, categories, aspect, optional variant).
Reviewer confirms colon segments express hierarchy and any dot segment is a lateral variant of the aspect, not a deeper level.
verifier_detail: Grammar: {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})?. Visual: theme : category : subcategory : aspect . variant — colons = HIERARCHY (vertical depth), dot = VARIANT (lateral facet); theme = NAMESPACE.

Components (term name_component, label 'Name components': the four grammar parts of an artifact name): theme = top-level architectural theme, kebab-case ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, required, exactly 1; category = hierarchical path segment navigating down the resource tree, kebab-case, optional, 0+; aspect = the final leaf resource noun, kebab-case, required, exactly 1; variant = lateral variation/facet/state of the aspect, kebab-case, optional, typically 0-1.

Source examples (valid): commons:ux:foundations:color (theme->subsystem->category->item); commons:identifiers.uuid (aspect + variant); commons:ux:foundations:color.primary (deep hierarchy + variant); orders:checkout (simple form: theme:aspect).
Component examples (positive): theme=commons; category=foundations; aspect=color; variant=primary.
Scope: check artifact names wherever they appear (any document type), including references to existing artifacts, not only newly created names.
